title: Carry planning authority in plan.propose
description: OBJECTIVE: close the existing command-contract hole that makes production unable to receive an actual PlanRevision or AcceptanceContract body; today's PlanProposeCommand carries only submissionHash and an opaque readiness witness. HARD DEPENDENCY: task-dc21cb4a8f2a4c1c902f3bf3a82a59c2 must be DONE. DELIVERABLE: the existing @moe/core plan.propose command admits exactly one canonical planning-authority submission containing both prerequisite records while keeping the RuntimeCommandKind unchanged; parsing delegates to the production codecs and the reducer/event surface retains their exact server-bindable identities. NOT IN SCOPE: daemon persistence, authentication/registry edits, approval activation, or readers. VERIFICATION: `pnpm --filter @moe/core test` must execute with nonzero counts.
definitionOfDone: PlanProposeCommand has one exact, bounded authority field carrying canonical PlanRevision and AcceptanceContract records; legacy hash/ref fields cannot disagree with the recomputed record digests.

The production parser rejects missing, duplicate, extra, accessor/proxy, malformed, noncanonical, hash/ref-mismatched, or caller-forged approval data with exact upstream or command-contract code/layer.
The planning reducer/event output preserves the admitted plan revision identity and criteria digest/ref needed for durable envelope construction without embedding execution authority.

Focused tests include a nonempty accepted command and positive-count hostile/mismatch cases; every refusal pins the specific production code/layer and a mutation of each binding reddens its named assertion.
`pnpm --filter @moe/core test` exits 0 with nonzero Test Files/Tests counts, affected production files stay <=250, and the existing plan.propose wire kind remains unchanged.
taskRails: Do not mint a new RuntimeCommandKind or add daemon/HTTP code.
Do not accept an approval state or digest supplied independently of the canonical records.
If the 249-line planning-command-contract.ts would cross 250, extract the authority parser into a focused sibling rather than grow it.

TWO MEASURED HAZARDS carried into step 2:
(a) IDEMPOTENCY SHORT-CIRCUIT. propose() returns accepted at :121-124 when state.submissionHash already matches, BEFORE sealPlan. If the authority check lived in sealPlan, a re-propose carrying a FORGED authority with a matching submissionHash would be admitted unchecked. The carry is therefore computed at the TOP of propose(), above that return, and gets its own test arm.
(b) PLAN_REVISION_NONCANONICAL / ACCEPTANCE_CONTRACT_NONCANONICAL are UNREACHABLE from a record-carrying (non-bytes) field: the parser encodes before it decodes, so the bytes it decodes are canonical by construction. I will not fake that arm. Reachable canonicalization refusals are asserted instead — non-NFC text (plan-revision-contract.ts:136 and acceptance-contract.ts:114 both refuse `value.normalize("NFC") !== value`) -> *_MALFORMED@*_ADMISSION — plus a positive control that hostile key ORDER still admits to byte-identical canonical output.
